```{python}
#| label: threelead-external-setup
import pandas as pd
import plotly.express as px
from live_results import *

LUDB = source_path("results/ecgaim_ludb_semiseg_blinded/compact.sqlite")
RDB_BLIND = source_path("results/ecgaim_rdb_semiseg_blinded/compact.sqlite")
RDB_ORACLE = source_path("results/ecgaim_rdb_oracle/ecgaim_rdb_oracle.sqlite")
le, lb = load_blinded(LUDB, "LUDB")
re, rb = load_blinded(RDB_BLIND, "RDB")
oracle = load_oracle(RDB_ORACLE, "RDB oracle")
```

## Completion, selection, and protocol boundaries

```{python}
#| label: threelead-external-provenance
display(source_inventory({"LUDB blinded": LUDB, "RDB blinded": RDB_BLIND,
                          "RDB oracle": RDB_ORACLE}))
display(pd.DataFrame([
    {"study": "LUDB blinded", "rows": len(le), "models": le.model_id.nunique(),
     "complete": int(le.status.eq("complete").sum())},
    {"study": "RDB blinded", "rows": len(re), "models": re.model_id.nunique(),
     "complete": int(re.status.eq("complete").sum())},
    {"study": "RDB oracle", "rows": len(oracle), "models": oracle.model_id.nunique(),
     "complete": int(oracle.status.eq("complete").sum())},
]))
```

LUDB covers 123 ECG-AIM masks plus the measured-signal baseline. RDB blinded
covers 31 promoted checkpoints plus the baseline; RDB oracle covers the same 31
trained models over 2,398 records. These denominators differ by design and must
not be presented as equally exhaustive architecture sweeps. The live LUDB
oracle SQLite path is zero bytes; no symmetric queryable LUDB-oracle result is
claimed.

## Blinded top-level metrics

```{python}
#| label: threelead-blinded-results
blinded = pd.concat([le, re], ignore_index=True)
display(blinded.sort_values(["cohort", "model_id"]))
metrics = [c for c in ["signal_pearson_p05", "signal_mse_p95",
                        "primary_mean_micro_f1_20ms", "duration_seconds"] if c in blinded]
display(leaderboard(blinded, metrics, id_col="model_id", group_cols=("cohort",), k=TOP_K))
if {"signal_pearson_p05", "primary_mean_micro_f1_20ms"}.issubset(blinded):
    fig = px.scatter(blinded, x="signal_pearson_p05", y="primary_mean_micro_f1_20ms",
                     color="cohort", hover_name="model_id", hover_data=["signal_mse_p95"],
                     title="Blinded waveform-tail versus six-boundary performance")
    fig.show()
```

## All six blinded boundaries

```{python}
#| label: threelead-boundaries
display(lb.sort_values(["model_id", "boundary"]))
display(rb.sort_values(["model_id", "lead_group", "boundary"]))
for cohort, frame, groups in [
    ("LUDB", lb, ("boundary",)),
    ("RDB", rb, ("lead_group", "boundary")),
]:
    display(leaderboard(frame, numeric_metrics(frame), id_col="model_id",
                        group_cols=groups, k=TOP_K))
```

Both protocols report onset/offset events. RDB additionally stratifies lead
groups. F1 at 20 ms, event counts, 150-ms matching, timing bias, MAE, and p95
answer different questions; conditional timing errors are not substitutes for
missed-event sensitivity.

## RDB oracle metric inventory and raw model summaries

```{python}
#| label: rdb-oracle-results
display(oracle.sort_values("model_id"))
display(pd.DataFrame([
    {"table": name, "rows": tables(RDB_ORACLE).get(name, 0)}
    for name in ["record_role_signal_metrics", "record_role_wave_metrics",
                 "record_role_st_metrics", "lead_wave_summaries"]
]))
oracle_metrics = numeric_metrics(oracle, "metric.")
display(leaderboard(oracle, oracle_metrics, id_col="model_id", k=TOP_K))
```

Oracle summaries include signal Pearson/MSE/MAE/derivative error, wave-window
correlation and amplitude error, onset/offset error, signed and absolute area,
and J/J60/ST metrics stratified by rhythm, lead role, lead, and wave. Oracle
access is diagnostic evidence; it does not replace the blinded selection
protocol.

## Cross-cohort transport among the 31 shared models

```{python}
#| label: threelead-cross-cohort
shared = (le.query("model_id != '__original__'")
          .merge(re.query("model_id != '__original__'"), on="model_id",
                 suffixes=("_ludb", "_rdb")))
shared_metrics = ["signal_pearson_p05", "signal_mse_p95",
                  "primary_mean_micro_f1_20ms"]
transport_rows = []
for metric in shared_metrics:
    pair = shared[[f"{metric}_ludb", f"{metric}_rdb"]].dropna()
    transport_rows.append({
        "metric": metric, "shared_models": len(pair),
        "Pearson": pair.iloc[:, 0].corr(pair.iloc[:, 1]),
        "Spearman": pair.iloc[:, 0].corr(pair.iloc[:, 1], method="spearman")})
display(pd.DataFrame(transport_rows))

fig = px.scatter(shared, x="primary_mean_micro_f1_20ms_ludb",
                 y="primary_mean_micro_f1_20ms_rdb", hover_name="model_id",
                 color="factorial_mask_ludb", trendline="ols",
                 title="Boundary-F1 transport across LUDB and RDB")
fig.show()
```

Boundary ranking transports moderately well: Spearman correlation is 0.736
across the 31 shared trained models. Waveform-tail ranking transports much less
well: Pearson-p05 Spearman is 0.300 and MSE-p95 Spearman is −0.026. Dataset
differences reorder models far more strongly for waveform fidelity than for
downstream delineation retention.

This comparison is conditional on promotion. The 31 RDB models are a selected
subset of the 123 LUDB candidates, so the correlation does not estimate
transport for the full architecture space and may be range-restricted.

## Retention relative to the measured-signal reference

```{python}
#| label: threelead-reference-gaps
reference_rows = []
for cohort, frame in [("LUDB", le), ("RDB", re)]:
    reference = frame.query("model_id == '__original__'").iloc[0]
    trained = frame.query("model_id != '__original__'")
    for metric in shared_metrics:
        direction = metric_direction(metric)
        best = trained.sort_values(metric, ascending=(direction == "min")).iloc[0]
        favorable_gap = ((reference[metric] - best[metric]) if direction == "min"
                         else (best[metric] - reference[metric]))
        reference_rows.append({"cohort": cohort, "metric": metric,
                               "reference": reference[metric],
                               "best_model": best.model_id,
                               "best_reconstruction": best[metric],
                               "favorable_gap_vs_reference": favorable_gap})
display(pd.DataFrame(reference_rows))
```

On RDB, the best reconstructed boundary result is 0.7404 versus 0.7430 on the
measured signal, a gap of 0.0026. On LUDB, the best reconstruction is 0.6302
versus 0.6938, a gap of 0.0636. The smaller RDB gap is encouraging for retaining
the downstream delineator's events, but does not mean the true waveform was
recovered: RDB signal Pearson p05 remains at most 0.638.

The measured-signal row is a protocol reference, not a trainable competitor.
Its Pearson of 1 and MSE of 0 are identities, while its boundary F1 is below 1
because the fixed delineator itself is imperfect. Boundary retention can
approach the reference even when waveform fidelity remains limited.

## Oracle endpoint disagreement and Pareto selection

```{python}
#| label: threelead-oracle-pareto
oracle_focus = [c for c in [
    "metric.signal_pearson_p05", "metric.signal_mse_p95",
    "metric.boundary_voltage_abs_error_record_p95_mv",
    "metric.qrs_window_rmse_record_p95_mv",
    "metric.qrs_absolute_area_error_record_p95_mv_ms",
    "metric.t_window_rmse_record_p95_mv",
    "metric.t_absolute_area_error_record_p95_mv_ms",
    "metric.st_j_abs_error_record_p95_mv"] if c in oracle]
oracle_leaders = []
for metric in oracle_focus:
    best = oracle.sort_values(metric, ascending=(metric_direction(metric) != "max")).iloc[0]
    oracle_leaders.append({"metric": metric, "leader": best.model_id,
                           "value": best[metric]})
display(pd.DataFrame(oracle_leaders))

ranks = pd.DataFrame({"model_id": oracle.model_id})
for metric in oracle_focus:
    ranks[metric] = oracle[metric].rank(
        ascending=(metric_direction(metric) != "max"), method="min")
ranks["mean_endpoint_rank"] = ranks[oracle_focus].mean(axis=1)
display(ranks.sort_values("mean_endpoint_rank"))
```

Different checkpoints lead signal correlation, boundary-voltage error, QRS
window error, QRS area, T-window error, T area, and ST/J error. No checkpoint is
the oracle winner on every endpoint. Mean rank is a diagnostic summary, not a
validated clinical utility function or substitute for a predeclared hierarchy.

## External claim ledger

| Claim | Verdict | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| Model ranking transports from LUDB to RDB | Partially | Boundary-F1 rank correlation is 0.736; waveform-tail correlations are weak. |
| A reconstruction matches the measured waveform | Contradicted | Signal Pearson remains below 1 and MSE above 0 in both cohorts. |
| RDB delineation is nearly retained | Supported for the fixed delineator | Best F1 is 0.7404 versus reference 0.7430; this is event retention, not waveform identity. |
| One model is globally best | Not supported | Leaders differ across cohorts, boundaries, waveform tails, QRS/T morphology, and ST/J endpoints. |
| Oracle access validates blinded selection | No | Oracle results diagnose failure modes but cannot retroactively serve as blinded selection evidence. |
| The RDB subset represents all 123 LUDB models | No | It is a promoted 31-model subset subject to selection and range restriction. |

## Remaining limits

Principal checkpoints use seed 42. Cohorts have different annotations and
distributions, and the RDB subset was selected rather than exhaustive.
Aggregate summaries do not provide paired uncertainty for every model contrast.
These results support external morphology-retention and failure-analysis claims,
not clinical equivalence or waveform identifiability.
